news.title: World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage
news.lede: World Cup referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi to calm down his out-of-control team-mate Leandro Paredes during the tournament's final. The Argentina captain was tasked with keeping Paredes on the field before the violent scenes he sparked come the full-time whistle. Paredes spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Spain star Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Barcelona ace Gavi. The 32-year-old only entered the match at half-time, but was fortunate to stay on the pitch.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops retirement bombshell after World Cup heartbreak
news.lede: See more of our coverage in your search results. Fans better cherish what’s to come because it may just be Cristiano Ronaldo’s swan song. In an exclusive interview with Vogue alongside his wife Georgina Rodríguez about their wedding, the Portuguese soccer star admitted “this is probably my last year of football.” “I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” he continued to the outlet.

news.title: Risky Ronald Araujo swoop is an act of pure desperation from Liverpool: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: Newcastle win £30million race for World Cup star – and now eye up transfer hijack
news.lede: The 23-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international will undergo a medical with the Magpies on Sunday. It is believed that the deal is worth £30million, with Newcastle beating several clubs – including from the Premier League – to Dedic's signature. The former Red Bull Salzburg player, who can operate in both full-back positions, has made 46 appearances for Benfica since joining the Portuguese giants last summer. He also played three games at the 2026 World Cup as Bosnia reached the knockout stage for the first time.

news.title: Spanish World Cup-winner Jenni Hermoso leaves Mexican club Tigres
news.lede: The 36-year-old forward, who has played 125 times for Spain, joined Tigres in 2024, having spent 18 months with another Mexican club, Pachuca. Prior to that, she played for Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain. "I’m leaving Tigres very happy with everything I’ve experienced, but also sad, of course, because I don’t like saying goodbye, while knowing full well that this is the best thing that has ever happened to me in life," a tearful Hermoso said in a video posted on X. Her departure comes three years after the Luis Rubiales affair, which deeply affected her career and Spanish football.

news.title: New Zealand Football withdraws support for Infantino, urges review
news.lede: New Zealand Football said on Friday it had withdrawn support for FIFA boss Gianni Infantino and called for an independent review into his aborted plan to sell off part of the World Cup. Infantino came under renewed fire this week in an open letter signed by three confederations -- UEFA, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC -- accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception". It is believed they want the Swiss official to resign before he has the chance to seek re-election in March next year. New Zealand Football became the latest FIFA member to withdraw support on Friday.

news.title: It's a middle-class sport now: Rising costs are forcing migrant kids out of football
news.lede: During the four years that he spent working as the sporting director as Hearts, Joe Savage encountered numerous children from refugee, asylum seeker and ethnic minority communities who had aspirations to become professional footballers one day. Savage, who has also worked in talent identification and recruitment with Hamilton Academical in Scotland and Norwich City and Preston North End in England, was invariably impressed with their mentality and ability when he did so. “Kids who have come over to this country with their families and had ambitions to play the game for a living have always got great attitudes in my experience,” he said. “They want to adapt, they want to do the very best they can.

news.title: Ronaldo drops retirement bombshell after World Cup heartbreak: ‘My last year of football’
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo hints this could be his final season, reflecting on World Cup heartbreak, legacy, family life and his future beyond football.
